scope: Five selected artworks, raw sources, options, palette and metadata after visual QA. Coordinator accepted the first material sample unchanged. Lane B validated the full source candidate and rendered the exact app selector and native layouts.

artworkProvenance.prompt: WHITEGROOVE SANDHILLS for Glaze. One original isolated whole flat image of a recognizable Great Plains specimen in the physical print language of one hand-carved WHITE-LINE COLOR WOODBLOCK. Carving shallow broad V grooves in one block creates a connected network of cream UNINKED PAPER channels separating several broad hand-brushed pigment fields. At print stage the colored faces transfer uneven thin matte layers, while the visible negative channels remain the exact natural warm ivory paper color. Make these pale interior lines visually unmistakable and continuous across several substantial color junctions, with slight irregular gouge swelling, occasional flat chamfer or gentle tapered finish, and connected fork passages. Small count of large flat strong matte translucent watercolor or gouache fields with restrained light pressure-grain at their edges. Keep clean no dark contour. The print looks hand pulled: gentle block drag, even paper tooth, a few low-contrast blotchy ink variations inside broad color fields. No strong exposed wood grain, screenprint dots, fiber grid, gritty flecks, collage or relief buildup. The visible internal channels are continuous real pale paper among flat pigments, not white chalk outlines or gaps cut to transparent background. Only the region outside the entire recognizable subject silhouette is genuinely transparent. Avoid off-white outer sticker stroke, torn card or rag deckle silhouette. Completely planar matte surface, no material thickness, stone slabs, grout, enamel, stained glass, deep cast shadow, relief laminations, digital crisp double white strokes, ceramic shimmer, airbrush color ramps or wood texture shading. One clean whole articulated and unmistakable specimen composition, bold enough for 85 pixels. Natural lightweight aesthetic. Generous pure transparent margin. No border, rectangle, ground rectangle, lettering, maker mark, panel or UI. FIRST SUBJECT: one whole recognizable WESTERN MEADOWLARK from left front profile near ground level, upright but a chunky round-shouldered grassland bird with broad flattened forehead, medium-long slender pointed bill, short rufous/grey tail, and one clearly visible dark small eye. One short naturally attached dry grass twig or cropped wooden fence-top with enough height only to show its TWO natural gripping feet and separate toes. Entire bill, feathers and feet whole. Large bold warm yellow throat and breast preserve the genuine continuous sharply inked BLACK V bib, with pale uninked cut channels around the black band separating it from the golden chest. Print the upper folded wing and back in three distinct broad buff/sage-grey muted ink fields with two or three irregular clear cream paper divisions. The folded wing is recognizably a single anatomical panel; only two dark brown short field accents, no detailed fine feather hatch, barred waterfowl patterns or blue bird colors. Head absolutely rounded with a flat forehead and thin long bill, restrained pale brow. Use between six and ten large fields across the whole image. No white outer contour, no decoration outside the bird and little perch. Make actual linseed-toned warm printed paper seamless inside its ivory carve grooves.
